name: CapCut Outline Reveal Chroma Text
use_when: A social edit needs outlined duplicate words to reveal around or behind a person.
The editor wants a bold title treatment that combines filled text, outline text, and subject cutout depth.
The shot has enough separation for foreground background removal and readable text edges.
avoid_when: The foreground subject edge is too messy for background removal.
The text color or chroma matte leaves edge specks.
The phrase is too long for filled and outline versions to remain readable.
The effect would cover the face, captions, product, UI, or proof.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_video -> duplicate_video_top -> custom_remove_subject -> filled_text_layer -> outline_text_layer -> duplicate_text_layers_above -> add_matching_stroke -> recolor_fill_to_key_green -> compound_text_layers -> chroma_key_green_fill -> layer_order_qc
timeline_pattern.cutout_rule: Use the subject cutout to create depth, but reject the effect if the edge fails in motion.
timeline_pattern.outline_rule: The outline and fill layers should share color logic so the reveal reads as one designed word system.
timeline_pattern.chroma_rule: Use the key color only as a removable matte, then check for specks and spill at phone size.

motion.rule: Animate or stagger the outline/fill only if the word remains readable and the subject edge stays clean.

keyframe_values.cutout_edge_start: CapCut Custom Removal can start with Feather 5 and Expansion 5, then tune per clip.
keyframe_values.stroke_thickness: A stroke thickness around 5 can work for clean white outline text; around 8 can be a starting point for larger bold versions, then adjust by font size.
keyframe_values.duplicate_layers: Use duplicated fill/outline text layers only when each copy has a clear reveal role.

sound.rule: Use a small reveal tick or hit only on the visible outline/fill reveal frame and keep it below speech.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions in the same region if the reveal text carries the line; restore captions after the effect clears.

color.rule: Key-green fill is a matte step, not final color; final text edges must remain crisp after chroma key.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use a subject alpha matte above duplicate filled/outlined text layers, chromakey the fill matte color where needed, and inspect edge frames for halo and specks.
implementation.remotion: Represent OutlineRevealText with baseVideo, subjectMaskRef, fillText, outlineText, strokeWidth, keyColor, chromaTolerance, and edgeReviewFrames.
implementation.blender: Use foreground roto/masks, text objects with fill and stroke materials, and key/matte compositing to reveal text behind the subject.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place video and duplicate it, use Remove Background or Custom Removal on the top copy, add filled text and outline text, duplicate those text layers above when needed, add matching Stroke, recolor fill to a key green, compound the text layers, apply Chroma Key to remove the green fill, and review layer order. For a subject-only foreground, select only the subject in Custom Removal so the outline wraps behind that subject rather than the whole frame.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Duplicate video, roto/mask subject in Premiere or After Effects, place filled and outlined Essential Graphics text between base and foreground layers, use Ultra Key or track mattes for any key-color removal.

common_mistakes: Leaving green matte specks after chroma key.
Using a thin font or small stroke so the outline reveal disappears.
Trusting the subject cutout without checking hair, hands, and motion blur.
Duplicating text layers without knowing which one is fill, outline, matte, or reveal.
Letting the outline stack cover captions, faces, product UI, or proof.
qc: Are fill, outline, stroke, and matte layers named or otherwise distinguishable?
Does chroma key remove the matte color without specks or spill?
Does the subject cutout edge stay clean through motion?
Is the outlined word readable at phone size?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, products, and action remain safe?
